column1: # One row per durable-write call site that does NOT acquire the per-index
# teardown guard earlier in its own scope. This is the only place such a site may
# be declared, and the gate fails on any site that is neither guarded nor listed
# here — so an omission is a red gate, not a silent gap.
#   scope        innermost `fn` name, plus `+spawn` when the call is inside a
#                spawned task body. The gate prints the exact scope string for
#                any site it rejects, so a new row is copy-paste, not guesswork.
#   disposition  CALLER:<fn>  the guard is held by an ancestor named <fn>, which
#                             must exist in a scanned file that acquires a guard.
#                EXEMPT       deliberately unguarded; the reason says why.
# A row that stops matching an unguarded site FAILS as stale. Delete it when the
# site becomes guarded; update it when the site moves.

column5: Inner step of CodeIndexer::remove_file. Every caller of remove_file is an entry point that already holds the guard (the remove-file core, the watcher, boot reconcile); taking it again here would be the same lock twice on one path.
Same inner step as the row above, on the variant that skips the symbol-graph rebuild.
Inner call of CodeIndexer::index_file, the choke point every guarded entry point routes through — the index-file core, the watcher, and boot reconcile all hold the guard across it.
Batch ingest fast path, reached only from the reindex pipeline; run_reindex holds the shared side for the whole run.

Startup schema migration. The guard is taken inside the spawned task in commands/start/daemon.rs and held for the whole per-index migration (#3049 round 4) — this is the path three review rounds missed.
Reindex pipeline batch commit, inside run_reindex's guarded span; it also holds INDEX_LOCKS.
Reindex completion step, inside run_reindex's guarded span.
Clears the checkpoint on the STAGING corpus during promotion, inside run_reindex's guarded span. The spawn_blocking is awaited, so it cannot outlive the guard.
Fallback clear on the released staging file, also inside run_reindex's guarded span and also awaited. It writes the staging file, not the live corpus directory.
The deferred-embed queue worker takes the guard before dispatching the pass (defer_embed_queue.rs).
Force-reindex hash-cache clear, called from inside run_reindex's guarded span.

Assigns the indexer's in-memory root_path field under the indexer write lock. No corpus bytes are written, so a concurrent teardown costs a stale field on a handle about to be dropped, not a partial write.
Same in-memory field assignment as the row above, on the refusal path.
In-memory root_path assignment under the indexer write lock; writes no corpus bytes. The reindex it queues takes the guard through run_reindex.

The redb write runs in a spawn_blocking closure, so the gate treats it as deferred. It is not: the core AWAITS that join handle while holding the guard it took at the top (#6285 slice 4 renamed this scope from ingest_graph_handler), so the closure cannot outlive the guard. CAUTION when editing that line: the closure is brace-less (move || corpus.save_contrib_graph(&contrib)), which the gate cannot see as deferred on its own — it is caught only because the inline spawn_blocking( shares the line. Binding it to a variable first drops the site out of the gate entirely and makes this row fail as stale. See KNOWN LIMITS in check_teardown_guard.sh.

Inner step of reconcile_after_rescan, which is its only caller and takes the guard at the top of the pass, before the walk, and holds it across this call. Taking it again here would be the read side twice on one task: tokio's RwLock is write-preferring, so once a concurrent DELETE queues for the write side the second read parks behind that writer while this task still holds the first read, and the pass deadlocks.
